item.title: C++ Array Initialization: Setting All Elements to Non-Zero Values
item.description:
“C++ Array Initialization: Setting All Elements to Non-Zero Values”

When declaring a fixed-size array in C or C++, using {value} initializes the first element to value and all subsequent elements to zero if the size is explicitly specified and the initialization list is shorter. What recourse exists when the requirement is to set all elements to a specific non-zero constant, like -1 or 42? Standard C-style initialization offers limited direct syntactic options for this purpose, pushing developers toward algorithms, extensions, or alternative data structures.

item.title: Efficient C Array Initialization: Methods and Examples
item.description:
“Efficient C Array Initialization: Methods and Examples”

Initializing Arrays in C and C++

Initializing arrays in C and C++ can be approached in several ways, each with its own advantages depending on the context, such as the value to be assigned, the array size, and whether the initialization is static or dynamic. Let’s explore the common and advanced methods.

Direct Initialization and Default Values

The most straightforward method is direct initialization with a list of values. If the provided initializer list is shorter than the array size, the remaining elements are initialized to zero. A special case allows initializing all elements to zero with a single {0}.
